form.title: iTop incidents
form.intro: McHarbor creates an iTop ticket, logs repeats in its private log, and assigns then resolves it when the alert recovers, following the iTop lifecycle.
form.name: Channel name
form.lifecycleHelp: iTop only resolves assigned tickets. McHarbor assigns a still-new ticket to this team and agent before resolving it, and fills the fields iTop requires in the resolved state.

guide.title: Connect iTop
guide.step1: Create a contact and a user account for McHarbor with the REST Services User profile plus a profile that can create, update and resolve incidents in your organization.
guide.step2: On iTop 3.1 or later, create an application token for that user under Admin tools, Application tokens (or a personal token), and choose token authentication here.
guide.step3: Note the IDs of the team, of an agent who is a member of that team, and of the service McHarbor should use when resolving. iTop requires all three to resolve an incident.
guide.step4: Save and click Test connection. McHarbor checks the organization, that the agent belongs to the team, and that the service exists, and creates nothing.
guide.step5: For status updates, open this channel again and, under Ticket status from the ITSM, click Create inbound URL and copy the URL and the signing secret, which are shown once. In iTop, create a Remote application connection that uses header authentication with the header X-McHarbor-Secret set to that secret.
guide.step6: Create a Webhook action (Combodo Webhook Integration) with the inbound URL, method POST, the header Content-Type: application/json, and the payload template below.
guide.step7: Create a Trigger on object update for Incident with the filter SELECT Incident WHERE title LIKE '%[MH-%', and link it to the action. Without it, McHarbor polls open tickets.
guide.payloadTitle: Payload template for the Webhook action
